title: 1956 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Which one of the following combinations of given parts does not determine the indicated triangle?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
base angle and vertex angle; isosceles
triangle

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: vertex angle and the base; isosceles triangle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
the radius of the circumscribed circle; equilateral
triangle

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
one arm and the radius of the inscribed circle; right
triangle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
two angles and a side opposite one of them; scalene
triangle

solutions.text:
In an isosceles triangle, a base angle and the vertex angle determine all three angles, but no side length is specified. Therefore triangles of every scale have the same given data, so the triangle is not determined. Each other choice includes enough length information, directly or through a radius, to fix the scale as well as the shape.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Ask whether each set of information fixes scale as well as shape
Two angles determine only a similarity class unless some length is also supplied
